headline: Attackers drained millions from cryptocurrency wallets through weak-randomness and hardware flaws as a fresh voice-phishing wave hijacked Microsoft 365 accounts and Microsoft warned AI is shrinking the window to patch.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are hunting the keys to cryptocurrency directly, chaining weak-randomness bugs like Ill Bloom, laser attacks on Tangem cards, and poisoned developer packages to drain wallets rather than break into exchanges.

Microsoft's own warning that AI shrinks the patch window echoed across the day, as machine-speed exploitation and hallucination-squatting abuse push defenders to deploy updates faster than they ever have.
Voice-phishing crews are graduating from stealing passwords to hijacking passkey enrollment itself, with Okta's O-UNC-066 calling employees directly to seize Microsoft 365 accounts for extortion.

topics.title: Crypto Wallet Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Coinspect disclosed Ill Bloom, a weak-randomness flaw in wallet recovery-phrase generation that attackers used to drain more than $5 million starting with a coordinated May 27 sweep, Ledger's Donjon team showed a precisely timed laser pulse resets the password on Tangem wallet cards that cannot be patched, and threat actors who compromised Injective Labs' GitHub pushed a malicious npm package, @injectivelabs/sdk-ts@1.20.21, that steals wallet keys and seed phrases.
topics.summary: Cryptocurrency holders face converging attacks on the seed phrases and hardware cards that control their funds. Owners should verify wallet software versions, avoid the compromised Injective SDK build, and treat any recovery phrase generated by weak software as already burned.

sources.title: Attackers Exploit 'Ill Bloom' Vulnerability to Drain Over $5 Million From Cryptocurrency Wallets
Laser Attack Resets Tangem Wallet Passwords on Cards That Can't Be Patched
Injective Labs GitHub Compromise Pushes Wallet-Key-Stealing npm Packages

topics.title: AI Shrinks the Patch Window
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft told organizations on July 10 to shorten how quickly they deploy monthly Windows updates, warning that AI now cuts the time attackers need to weaponize a freshly patched flaw, a message it paired with its July Secure Future Initiative progress report as its own Patch Tuesday volume topped 200 CVEs a month.
topics.summary: Microsoft is rewriting deployment guidance because AI compresses the gap between a patch shipping and a working exploit landing. Teams should tighten update rollout windows on devices where faster deployment will not disrupt operations.

sources.title: Microsoft is rewriting Windows patch guidance because of AI
Securing our future: July 2026 progress report on Microsoft's Secure Future Initiative
July 2026 Patch Tuesday forecast: Is CVE tracking still practical?

topics.title: Vishing Passkey-Enrollment Attacks on Microsoft 365
topics.latest_developments: Okta warned that a threat actor it tracks as O-UNC-066 is phoning employees across multiple sectors and steering them to phishing pages that mirror Microsoft Entra ID login screens, using a panel-controlled kit that hijacks the passkey-enrollment process to seize Microsoft 365 accounts for data extortion.
topics.summary: The campaign turns a phone call into full account takeover by tricking victims into enrolling an attacker-controlled Entra passkey. Organizations should restrict who can register authentication methods and train staff to reject unsolicited enrollment prompts.

sources.title: Okta Warns of Vishing Attacks Targeting Microsoft 365 Customers
Hackers Use Fake Microsoft Entra Passkey Enrollment to Gain Microsoft 365 Access

topics.title: Mass Web-Server Malware Operations
topics.latest_developments: Researchers found a cybercrime crew's own server exposed for three weeks, revealing WP-SHELLSTORM, a mass operation carrying a target list of more than 1.4 million WordPress sites, while a separate network of 200 GitHub repositories used a Go module to load PowerShell that pulls a resolver from public dead drops and runs Windows malware.
topics.summary: Two distinct operations show how attackers weaponize public infrastructure at scale, one backdooring WordPress sites and the other abusing GitHub as a malware loader. WordPress operators should audit for unauthorized shells and defenders should treat Go modules that fetch remote PowerShell as hostile.

sources.title: Exposed Hacker Server Reveals WP-SHELLSTORM Backdooring Thousands of WordPress Sites
Network of 200 GitHub Repositories Used for Malware Infection

topics.title: License Plate Surveillance After the Supreme Court
topics.latest_developments: The Record reported that automated license-plate-reader networks may face warrant requirements next after the Supreme Court reined in warrantless location tracking, a shift experts say would radically limit modern policing, as Bruce Schneier warned that AI-powered systems will soon track nearly everything people do in public and tie minor infractions to government records.
topics.summary: A Supreme Court limit on location tracking is spilling toward the camera networks that log every passing car, raising the prospect that ALPR searches will require warrants. Privacy advocates see a check on the automated public surveillance Schneier describes as inevitable.

sources.title: License plate cameras may be next target after Supreme Court reins in location tracking
AI Surveillance and Social Progress

topics.title: The Gentlemen Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 published the first detailed profile of The Gentlemen, a ransomware operation whose affiliate recruitment model is driving rapid growth in its victim count.
topics.summary: The Gentlemen is an emerging ransomware crew scaling through affiliates who share its tooling and split extortion proceeds. Defenders should fold its tradecraft into detection now while its operations are still expanding.

sources.title: No Manners Here: The Ruthless Rise of The Gentlemen Ransomware

business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump said the United States agreed to keep talking with Iran even as a senior U.S. official demanded Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz by Saturday or face consequences, and the administration grew increasingly pessimistic about any nuclear deal.
business_politics.summary: The fighting between the United States and Iran that resumed this week has stalled traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint for roughly a fifth of the world's oil, though Iran keeps rushing its own tankers through; oil futures closed the week higher on the standoff.

business_politics.title: Housing Bill Becomes Law Without Trump
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump said Friday, July 10, he will refuse to sign the landmark federal housing bill, and with his 10-day window expiring Saturday, the measure automatically becomes law.
business_politics.summary: Congress passed the bill to address voters' worries about housing affordability; Trump declined to either sign or veto it before his deadline, so it takes effect on Saturday, July 11, over his objection.

around_town.title: Parkway East Closure Begins
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT closed the Parkway East (I-376) at 9 p.m. Friday, July 10, launching the 25-day Commercial Street Bridge replacement, and Swissvale imposed around-the-clock parking restrictions that run until August 3.
around_town.summary: The closure between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and the Edgewood/Swissvale exit forces all through traffic off at Wilkinsburg or Forbes Avenue in Oakland; Allegheny County emergency crews will use restricted roads closed to other drivers to hold response times down, and PennDOT is livestreaming the demolition.

around_town.latest_developments: A congregation from Arlington, Virginia, gathered at Homewood Cemetery to dedicate a headstone for the Rev. Robert Simon Laws, 123 years after his burial in an unmarked grave.
around_town.summary: Laws escaped slavery and went on to lead several churches, including one in Pittsburgh; his grave sat unmarked until the rededication ceremony finally gave him a headstone.
